newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit-taking in medium and small-capitalised issues, including stocks in the banking sector, pulled the Jakarta index down on Monday despite increases in some heavily-capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The composite index fell 0.89 points, or 0.15 percent, to 601.13 points after hitting a high for the day of 604.17 points. Losers led gainers by 71 to 46, with 53 counters unchanged.
A Singapore-based broker said the market was likely to continue its correction on Tuesday on lack of foreign buying coupled with locally-led profit-taking.

"I doubt if the market will be able to sustain the index above 600 points on Tuesday because some local investors might continue taking profit after the sharp rise of the past week," another foreign broker said.
But some brokers said limited fresh buying of some first and secondliners could support the index around the 600 mark.
"Some investors are likely to continue in the uptrend with speculative buying of selected issues," a local analyst said.
Brokers said the lack of foreign buyers was partly due to holidays in Singapore and Malaysia on Monday.
Confectionary firm Mayora Indah topped the active list with around 14 million shares traded, rising 100 rupiah to 1,150 on what brokers said was fresh buying by local players.
Property firm Mas Murni Indonesia rose 25 to 950 rupiah on turnover of 13.6 million shares on continued market talk of a possible take-over by a Singapore firm.
Company official was not available for comment.
Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia rose 275 rupiah to 2,250 on a volume of 4.7 million shares.
A Miwon official told Reuters the rise could be due to expansion plans this year, but he declined to give details.
Bank BDNI, Bank Duta and Bank International Indonesia were among the losers on profit taking, brokers said.
Bank BDNI fell 100 rupiah to 1,900 on a volume of around four million shares after making significant gains last week on the back of the popular Bank Negara Indonesia offering.

Satellite and international telephone operator Indosat fell 100 rupiah to 6,925 on a volume of 1.2 million shares. Brokers said this was due to a continued sell-off after it announced its nine-month results last week.
Heavyweights Sampoerna, Bimantara Citra and Citra Marga were on the active list on limited foreign buying, brokers said.
Cigarette maker Sampoerna rose 850 rupiah to 24,850 on a volume of 342,000 shares following its recent announcement of a share split this month.
Brokers said Bimantara Citra and Citra Marga was actively traded on their fundamentals.
